Also, I think water recommendations are much too frequent for - established large snake plant and large zz plant.

Otherwise, I like the identifier tool (when it works) and the cheerful watering reminder list. 

I’d appreciate a Tips list-
If a plant and pot are much too large to lift for good drainage after watering? 

When amount of sunlight thru windows changes with the seasons? be sure to move plants closer or farther away from sunlight.

Which plants are most bothered by chlorinated tap water and what to do. (CornstalkDracaena) and ?

I entered every detail for each of my plants and followed the watering instructions and all my plants are overwatered and turning yellow. I’ve had these plants for 6+ years without issue and just wanted a reminder to water them on time. 
I also wanted to ensure I was giving the right amount of water. I even reduced the amount of water for each plant that the app suggested. I typically used 1/4 cup for my chinese evergreen and the app suggested 1 1/4 cup. I even hit the snooze button because my soil was too damp and my ever green has more limp yellow leaves than green. It’s not worth the $30 annual fee.

The app struggled to identify a couple of my plants, but with a quick Google search, I was able to identify them and add them into the app fairly easily do be warned that any of the features like notifications for water and fertilizing reminders only come with premium, which is a weekly subscription. It can also tell you about the sun intensity in your area, which is nice again only comes with premium. It took me about 30 minutes to add all 25 of my plants to the app. It auto generates names for each plant which you can change otherwise it just gives each of your plants an individual name. Please keep in mind other than tracking what types and how many plants you have you literally cannot do anything else on this app without premium you cannot update when they were last watered without going into each plant settings individually, and updating it but then it doesn’t keep a log Like it would with premium. It was honestly a lot of my time and effort just to find out that I have to pay money for the app to actually do anything it was promised.

Very good app, almost there!. This is an extraordinarily well-designed app with a nice feature set and an excellent overall user experience. Onboarding is straightforward, and adding plants is as pain-free as possible considering the number of variables involved in creating an accurate care plan for a plant. With that said, I've noticed a few things I think could make the experience even better, including: 

[Based on the UI/Ux, I'm working under the assumption this is a ReactNative app in the below points]

- performance optimization. I noticed after several minutes of use that the app was *really* taxing my device (15 Pro Max) as it got super hot and lost battery life at an alarming rate. This continued even when I wasn't in the camera view and/or the app was open but idle. Additionally, the wheel pickers would become increasingly laggy over time, until I finally had to quit and restart the app. I suspect that the "details" form, when accessed from the toast notification in camera view, mounts as a stack on top of the camera, but the camera module/components aren't unmounted when the view becomes inactive, and it eats a lot of the thread space the inputs need to operate. (I could be wrong about this, just a hunch)

- Image dataset for plant ident. seems negatively reinforcing and/or susceptible to incorrect user input. I added several plants of the same variety and noticed that by the third or fourth plant, the algorithm was presenting the pictures of the first few plants when I asked it to identify the next. this is generally a good design, however, without a sufficient base of correctly tagged images to work from, this design is prone to model collapse, at scale, it will start to coalesce around a smaller and smaller variety of plants as it recognizes a larger base of patterns as the same.

- It doesn't seem like ambient humidity trends are taken into account for watering schedules. I live in Houston, where the constant humidity makes root rot a constant threat to indoor and outdoor succulents. The generated watering schedule doesn't seem to account for the fact that in humid climates, optimal watering frequency can be half of what it would be in a dry climate. 

- I know this this would be wildly complex to develop, but I would love the ability to build a "plant" entry from multiple plants that share the same space. I have several succulents that all share a pot, and while they have similar watering requirements, their overall intake requirement is less than it would be if they didn't share soil. Inversely, they're fertilizer requirement is higher for the same reason. It would be rad if Greg could take in that information and spit out an adjusted care plan that takes all of that into account. 

Again, these are mostly knit-picks. Overall, I'm quite happy with the app and very impressed with the job y'all have done so far.
